summary.intent: Overhaul the agent-plugins repo's bug-hunter (Rust/TS) and proof/lambda agents using audit feedback and Claude 5 context-engineering guidance, then audit for regressions and consistency, and improve docs, diagrams and ADRs.
summary.outcome: Added new Rust hazard taxonomies, split monolithic reference files into per-agent slices, added trust-boundary/injection-resistance guidance, restored a dropped remediation_sketch field, fixed several semantic errors, and shipped ADRs plus README/ARCHITECTURE/walkthrough readability improvements, all pushed to main (3b0fa42).

repo: Agent files follow a 4-part structure: backstory (2-4 experiential sentences), goal (intent), judgment (failure modes), output (schema plus EARS rules). EARS belongs only in <output>.

Reference files are split by consumer: rust-hazards/typescript-hazards for scanner/adversary, *-smells for architect, *-tooling for mutator/remediator. rust.md and typescript.md are now thin indexes, and agents declare <load_first> blocks.
finding-report@1.json is a document-level schema; no agent documents who assembles the full wrapper (workspace, language, modules_scanned) from per-candidate adversary outputs.
plugin.json files declare consumes/produces arrays that shared/scripts/validate-wiring.sh checks (Bash 3.2 compatible).
Hazard references carry a 'Verdict signal' sub-field (confirmable vs dismissible evidence), distinct from the False positive check.
Superseded specs under docs/superpowers/specs and the research doc were deleted after the decisions were captured as ADRs in docs/adr/ (5 ADRs).

code.finding: Backstory has 4 sentences covering both the missed-caller-guard incident and the SAFETY-comment incident with a unified lesson (verdict without runtime proof). Judgment names shallow reading and comment-as-evidence as failure modes. Output includes a trust-boundary EARS rule and remediation_sketch in confirmed examples.
T7 Verdict signal must say dismissible only when the field is explicitly read and forwarded; presence in the parameter type alone is not sufficient.
Batch EARS rule must be phrased as writing candidates to an external file after each batch of 50 files, since a single LLM invocation cannot return partial results incrementally.

workflow: A grep-only compliance check is insufficient; the user pushed for reading content semantically, which found real contradictions (backstory false-positive/false-negative mix, examples missing required schema fields, EARS example mismatch).
A regression audit via git diff of earlier overhaul commits caught a silently dropped optional schema field (remediation_sketch) that downstream canon-architect consumes.
Parallel teammate agents worked well for independent doc edits with no commits, leaving the orchestrator to verify, delete and commit in one batch.
Check git status/unpushed commits before asking to push; the final 'Push' request was a no-op because the commit was already on main.

friction: User repeatedly had to push back on shallow analysis ('surface grep analysis', 'Are you completely sure?').
Proof-adversary backstory flip-flopped: SAFETY-comment sentence added, removed, then restored with new framing, leaving the CHANGELOG inconsistent in between.
'Do all the waves' was ambiguous; all four research waves were already done, so it had to be reinterpreted as the doc/ADR/diagram work.
A .DS_Store file was accidentally staged and had to be unstaged.
Context ran out mid-session and required compaction and resumption.
open_items: Boundary-tracer agent, a TS architect agent and a TS mutator agent (Stryker) were proposed but not built.
Document where the finding-report@1 wrapper document is assembled from per-candidate adversary outputs.
Verify the proof-scanner batch rule (200-file threshold, 50-file batches) against proof's real execution environment; the thresholds are arbitrary and assume a file-writing tool.
Consider making agent loading lazy (adversary loads only the relevant taxonomy section) and adding code before/after examples to hazard taxonomies per Claude 5 guidance.
Proposed taxonomy-to-agent dispatch matrix reframing by cognitive mode was only partly reflected in SKILL.md files; TS SKILL.md was not updated.
